discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in 178682bae4. A one-key Send captures the files attached at the press. Once the verdict arrives, it sends only those that are still attached, through a new `takeFiles(wanted)` on the pending-attachments hook. Files added during the wait stay on the composer with the draft being typed, and a file removed during the wait doesn't go out.

Covered by "leaves a file added during a one-key Send's wait on the composer when its verdict lands / when its verdict wait runs out" and "leaves out a file removed from the composer while a one-key Send waited for its verdict" in `use-verbs.test.tsx`, plus `use-pending-attachments.test.tsx` (now in `test:sidecar`).

**[P2] Apply provisioning suppression to the combined loader condition.** On a new cloud send, `beginPendingResponse` sets the optimistic marker. The coordinator emits `cloud_provisioning` through the partial-message stream before the full-state acknowledgement arrives; partial messages leave `turnState` unchanged, and that acknowledgement goes through the 50 ms state-post debounce. During this handoff, `forceShow` is still true and the provisioning message has `partial: false`, so `optimisticShow` below overrides this `false` and renders “Thinking…” alongside the progress card. This contradicts the intended suppression and adds an avoidable loader insertion/removal at startup.

Gate the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` on the provisioning tail, keeping the hook call unconditional. The added helper-only test misses this: rendering the full hook with a provisioning tail, stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` currently returns visible. Cover that combination, then verify an `api_req_started` successor can show the loader again.

Good catch, thanks. Fixed in f8d9ca206: the provisioning check now gates the combined condition passed to `useDebouncedLoaderVisibility` (`!cloudProvisioning && (optimisticShow || isWaitingForResponse || handoffToReasoningPending)`), and the hook call stays unconditional. I moved the check out of `computeIsWaitingForResponse` instead of duplicating it, so that helper matches main again.

I replaced the helper-only test with a full-hook test: a provisioning tail, a stale idle `turnState`, and `forceShow: true` keep the loader hidden, then an `api_req_started` successor shows it again. The test fails on the previous code (`expected true to be false`) and passes with the fix.

[P2] Preserve the draft when a newly started session is reopened from history

This cache uses the UI thread ID, but one runtime session can have two UI thread IDs. A new conversation starts as `thread_*` (page.tsx:204–206); `thread-started` records its runtime `sessionId` without changing that ID (desktop-app-state.ts:319–333). Opening its sidebar/history row dispatches `open-session`, which only looks for `session_${sessionKey(...)}` and creates another thread (desktop-app-state.ts:175–207).

Start a session in this window, type an unsent follow-up, switch to another session, then reopen the original sidebar row: the new pane reads a different Map key and opens empty. The draft remains stranded under the original thread ID. Clicking the current session's own sidebar row can do the same. The real reducer/hook probe reproduces the two IDs and empty composer. This is a missing path in the draft-preservation fix, not a claim that persistence worked on main.

Reuse the already-bound thread for the same session/environment, or give aliases one draft identity and migrate the draft when binding. Add a start → bind session ID → type follow-up → reopen through history regression, retaining isolation for identical session IDs in different environments.
